lesson.title: Meeting a New Vowel: Short O
lesson.subject: ela

contentBlocks.text: You've read words with short A and short I. Today, a third vowel: short O!

The short O sound is like the vowel sound in 'hot' or 'pot' — a short, open sound. Practice reading these short-O words by blending each sound: hot, pot, dog, hop. Notice how changing just the vowel sound (like in 'hot' vs. 'hit' vs. 'hat') changes the whole word, just like you practiced with short A and short I.
You now know three short vowel sounds — A, I, and O! Tomorrow we'll meet a new digraph, two letters that make one sound.

objectives: Recognize and produce the short O vowel sound
Blend and read short-O CVC words: hot, pot, dog, hop
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review short A and short I from last week.
2. Introduce short O using the 'hot'/'pot' example.
3. Blend hot, pot, dog, and hop together, slowly then faster.
4. Move to the worksheet: read, trace, and write each word.
5. Close by comparing 'hot', 'hit', and 'hat' — same consonants, three different vowels.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just two words (hot, pot) before adding dog and hop
Ready for more: ask the child to think of one more real short-O word
The hot/hit/hat comparison reinforces the vowel-swap insight from week 1 — a good moment to revisit it explicitly
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a reading, tracing, and writing activity — check that the child can produce the short O sound and blend all four words.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Completes the core short-vowel set (A, I, O) this early-literacy sequence has been building since Grade 1's first lesson, continuing directly from last week's short-I introduction.

worksheet.title: Meeting a New Vowel: Short O

generationData.instructions: Read each word by blending its sounds, trace it, then write it once more on your own.
